tasks.old_behavior: String values from pyconfig.h #define directives are returned in the config dictionary with surrounding double-quotes preserved. For example, '#define PY_BUILTIN_HASHLIB_HASHES "blake2,sha256"' would yield the value '"blake2,sha256"' (including the literal double-quote characters).
tasks.new_behavior: Enclosing double-quotes are stripped from string values via the new quoted_re regex. The same #define now yields 'blake2,sha256' (without the double-quote characters).
tasks.compatibility_reason: Code that consumes sysconfig output and relies on the old quoted-string format will observe changed values. This includes tools, build scripts, packaging systems, and any downstream code that calls get_config_vars() or get_config_var() and processes the returned string values — for example, code that manually strips quotes, checks for quote-prefixed values with .startswith('"'), or compares config values against quoted strings. Values that were previously double-quoted (e.g., PY_BUILTIN_HASHLIB_HASHES, any string-type pyconfig.h #define) now have a different format. This is a publicly exported API in __all__ and is consumed widely by Python's own build/test infrastructure and external tooling such as pip, setuptools, and virtualenv.
tasks.test_recommendation: Test that get_config_vars() and get_config_var() return unquoted values for all string-type config entries from pyconfig.h. Verify that downstream consumers (pip, setuptools, virtualenv, distlib) are not broken by the format change. Check that int-typed values are unaffected.
